# Stage 2 report: RAG with citations and evals

This report is in progress. Its sections are filled in as the stage 2 pipeline is built, and every number will come from a script in this repo.

The stage 1 report (structured extraction) is in [docs/reports/stage-1.md](docs/reports/stage-1.md).

## Retrieval metrics
<!-- retrieval:start (generated by `make eval-retrieval`; edits here are overwritten) -->

15 questions from `evals/retrieval_gold.toml`, no filters, top 10 chunks per search. Embedding model `google/embeddinggemma-300m`, reranker `BAAI/bge-reranker-v2-m3-int8`. Settings from config.toml, none tuned on these questions: 50 candidates per retriever, RRF k 60, BM25 k1 1.2 and b 0.75, 30 hybrid candidates reranked. A chunk is a hit when it comes from the evidence document and contains its quote; rules in docs/METRICS.md. One question is 1/15 of a recall value.

Default-setup rule (fixed before the run): on the `structure` collection, the highest MRR@10, then the higher recall@5, then the setup without a reranker. Result: **hybrid+rerank** (MRR@10 0.615). This choice is made on the gold set itself; no numeric setting was tuned on it.

Best on `fixed` by the same rule: hybrid+rerank (MRR@10 0.703), above the `structure` choice.

**Gold set (S2-09).** `evals/retrieval_gold.toml` holds 15 questions (en 6, uk 4, de 3, fr 1, it 1) over PDF, HTML, DOCX and Markdown documents. Each question names its evidence: document, section, page (PDF only) and a short exact quote (decision 16). A retrieved chunk counts as correct when it comes from the evidence document and contains the quote, with whitespace ignored. All 15 questions were drafted by Claude at the user's request (the user does not read German, French or Italian well) and reviewed by the user. `make retrieval-gold-check` confirms that every quote is in its document, on its page, and whole inside at least one chunk of both chunking strategies.

**How it is measured (S2-10).** `make eval-retrieval` runs each setup on both chunking strategies and scores the returned chunks with the gold-set hit rule; `docs/METRICS.md` defines recall@k and MRR. The table above is generated from `evals/results/retrieval.json`, and two runs give the same ranks. The search settings were committed in S2-07 and S2-08, before the gold set existed, and none was changed for this measurement. The one decision taken on these 15 questions is the default search setup, by the rule stated above: `make search` now reranks by default. The answer pipeline keeps the structure-aware chunks although fixed-size chunks score higher here: a fixed-size chunk is labelled with the section where it starts, and the answer usually sits in a later section, so a citation would name the wrong section.

**Section labels (S2-12).** `make section-labels` checks this without models. Every chunk that holds a gold quote carries the right section label for 15 of 15 questions with structure-aware chunks, against 4 of 15 with fixed-size chunks. Over the whole corpus, 6968 of 16236 (chunk, block) pairs of fixed-size chunks have the right label (42.9 %), against all 13015 for structure-aware chunks, which are right by construction. Rules in `docs/METRICS.md`, per-question detail in [evals/results/section_labels.md](evals/results/section_labels.md), and the full chunking rationale in the README.

## "I don't know" (refusal)
<!-- refusal:start (generated by `make eval-refusal`; edits here are overwritten) -->

20 development questions from `evals/dev_questions.toml` (8 answerable, 7 near_miss, 5 off_topic; languages en 8, uk 5, de 4, fr 2, it 1). Model `haiku-5.5`; search `structure`, hybrid + rerank (`BAAI/bge-reranker-v2-m3-int8`), best 10 hits, context budget 4000 estimated tokens, no filter. Every question is answered with the score gate off; the gate is applied afterwards. Rules in docs/METRICS.md. One question is 1/8 of an answerable rate and 1/12 of an unanswerable one, so small differences are noise.

Score-gate threshold (rule fixed before the run: the midpoint between the lowest top-1 reranker score of an answerable question and the highest top-1 score of an unanswerable question below it, rounded to 2 decimals; no gate if no unanswerable question scores below every answerable one. So the gate refuses no answerable development question.): **-1.03**. The gate refuses 9/20 (45%) of the questions before any model call.

| v1 | score gate only | 9/12 (75%) | 4/7 (57%) | 5/5 (100%) | 0/8 (0%) |
| v1 | gate or model | 12/12 (100%) | 7/7 (100%) | 5/5 (100%) | 0/8 (0%) |
| v2 | model only | 12/12 (100%) | 7/7 (100%) | 5/5 (100%) | 0/8 (0%) |

<!-- refusal:end -->

**How it works (S2-14).** `make ask` can refuse in two places. Before the model call, a score gate refuses when the best reranked chunk scores below `[answer] min_rerank_score`. After the call, the model can answer `not_in_documents`. The threshold and the answer prompt were chosen on 20 development questions (`evals/dev_questions.toml`, drafted by Claude at the user's request and reviewed by the user), which are kept apart from the gold set and the test set. The threshold rule was written down before the run (`docs/METRICS.md`). With it, the gate refuses no answerable development question by construction, so its false-refusal rate on new questions is still unmeasured (S2-16).

**What the numbers say.** The model's own status did the refusing: with the gate off, both prompt versions refused all 12 unanswerable questions and none of the 8 answerable ones. The gate refuses only the questions whose best chunk is clearly off topic. Three near misses (hydrogen, helium, HLP 68) score above two answerable questions, because their chunks state the same kind of fact for a neighbouring gas or product, so no threshold can separate them (`docs/ISSUES.md` I-010). The gate still matters: it skips the model call for 9 of the 20 questions, and it refuses even if the model would have answered. Prompt v2 did not change the refusals, but it fixed most of the language bug: v1 answered 5 of 8 English questions in German, v2 only 1 (`prompts/CHANGELOG.md`). `make ask` now uses v2 with the threshold -1.03 (user's choice). Twenty questions and one run per version: one question moves a rate by 5 to 12 points.

## Cost per 1000 questions
<!-- cost:start (generated by `make cost`; edits here are overwritten) -->

Model `haiku-5.5` at $0.10 in / $0.50 out per 1M tokens (config.toml, checked 2026-10-21); prompt answer v2; score gate -1.03 (`[answer] min_rerank_score`). From the development questions in `evals/results/refusal.json` (`make eval-refusal` run 2026-11-21T22:28:55+00:00), with the gate applied as `make ask` applies it: a gated question gets no model call. Each question that reaches the model costs its first call plus its repair call, if any. Rule in docs/METRICS.md.

| Questions | n | Mean prompt tokens | Mean output tokens | $ / 1000 (tokens x price) | $ / 1000 (reported) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| All development questions (9 gated cost $0) | 20 | - | - | $0.49 | $0.49 |
| Only those that reach the model | 11 | 8318 | 136 | $0.90 | $0.90 |

The development set is 12 of 20 unanswerable on purpose, and gated questions cost nothing, so the first row depends on that mix. The second row is the cost of a question the model answers or refuses itself. Embedding and reranking run on the local CPU: no API cost; hardware and time are not counted (time per query: [evals/results/retrieval.md](evals/results/retrieval.md)).

Per question: [evals/results/cost.md](evals/results/cost.md).

## Answer metrics
**Test set (S2-16).** `evals/test_set.toml` holds 24 questions for the answer scorers (S2-17 to S2-20): 8 answerable, 5 similar-document traps (a sibling document gives a similar value, e.g. NIST SRM 612 against 613), 5 outdated-version traps on the three old/new pairs (the current text is right, the superseded one wrong) and 6 unanswerable (4 near misses, 2 off-topic). Languages: en 8, de 4, uk 4, pl 2, es 2, sv 1, nl 1, fr 1, it 1. Each answerable question has evidence in the gold-set format and key facts, each traced to an evidence quote. Traps name the documents whose citation is wrong. All 24 questions and their expected answers were drafted by Claude at the user's request and reviewed by the user. They repeat no development or gold-set question, and nothing is tuned on them. `make test-set-check` checks every label against the corpus (rules in docs/METRICS.md).

<!-- answers:start (generated by `make eval`; edits here are overwritten) -->

24 test questions from `evals/test_set.toml` (8 answerable, 5 similar_doc, 5 outdated_version, 6 unanswerable; languages en 8, de 4, uk 4, pl 2, es 2, sv 1, nl 1, fr 1, it 1). Answered like `make ask`: model `haiku-5.5`, prompt answer v2; search `structure`, hybrid + rerank (`BAAI/bge-reranker-v2-m3-int8`), best 10 hits, context budget 4000 estimated tokens, score gate on at -1.03, no filter. Judges: model `haiku-5.5`, prompts judge_quality v1 and judge_faithfulness v1; one run, no temperature (the model takes none). Rules in docs/METRICS.md. One question is 1/24 of the overall rates and 1/5 to 1/8 of a category's, so small differences are noise.
